editorial.headline: Senior Living Is Nationally Open, but Closed to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: A commercial senior-living operation may be nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet Bali’s permanent risk-based moratorium blocks its PMA registration today.
editorial.body:
Senior living under this activity is commercial accommodation designed specifically for older residents. It combines housing with supporting facilities, professional caregivers and other professional staff, while taking account of the varied activities, needs and limitations that older people may experience. The scope also includes senior-oriented tourist accommodation. The defining proposition is therefore not ordinary lodging, but a managed living environment whose design and staffing respond to later-life needs.

The activity is available at the Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. That breadth matters because the classification accommodates operations from smaller enterprises through to large commercial facilities, without changing the core character of the activity: managed accommodation with dedicated support for older residents. The record places professional caregiving within the activity itself, alongside other professional roles and facilities intended to serve the residents’ practical circumstances.

For a foreign investor considering Bali, the decisive fact is stark: this activity cannot be registered there for PMA today. Nationally, it is TERBUKA with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, meaning full foreign ownership is open at the national level. Bali, however, applies a different result. At the Besar scale, the OSS risk classification is Low or Medium-Low across every scope in the record, placing the activity within Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium on PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk activities. The record locates that Bali restriction in the moratorium of May 2026. National openness does not override the Bali PMA restriction: this activity cannot be registered there for PMA today. For founders, the distinction is not a technical footnote but the central registration reality—nationally open in principle, but blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the province’s risk-based rule.
